note: TWO KINDS OF ROOM COVERAGE, AND A SPEC THAT PREDICTED THE OTHER ONE. The Rill Task 3 widened the channel network to the whole land flow tree. The plan predicted room coverage 0.1 percent to 1.6 percent, a 16x ratio. I measured centroid-in-Channel (what every shipped consumer reads - windows/locale describe, crossing_between and transverse_of all call bank_reading at addr.centroid()) and got 0.034 to 0.214 percent, a 6.4x ratio, and wrote in my report that the spec was 3x high because width goes as sqrt of discharge. THAT DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. Measuring CONTAINMENT instead - sample each polyline at room-edge/8 and collect distinct RoomAddr::containing(p, walk_depth).pack() - gives 0.0845 to 1.237 percent, a 14.6x ratio, which is the spec almost exactly. Containment scales with the NUMBER of rendered cells; area scales with the sum of sqrt(Q), and the added reaches are all headwaters. Both numbers are right and they answer different questions, so before you call a prediction wrong, check which quantity it was predicting. The gap between them is the real finding: 86 percent of the rooms a channel now passes through do not read as water at their centroid (was 66 percent), because a headwater half-width of 7.35e-6 rad is 1/38 of a 2.83e-4 rad room edge. Second technique from the same round: to get a trustworthy BEFORE arm, revert the one predicate and diff the byte golden against the saved pre-change copy - it came back byte-identical, so every pre number was provably from the network that shipped.
